text:
Alex: quick brain dump — thinking about adding an ephemeral-window shim that sits between enqueue and coalesce. idea is to let very bursty/long-tail tenants borrow small, time-boxed windows so they don't starve steady tenants
Priya: can you sketch the invariants? worried about complexity + correctness under preemptive flushes
Alex: main invariants: 1) ephemeral windows are size-limited by tokens and time, 2) they have weaker headroom guarantees, 3) they can be preempted by high-SLO lanes. if preempted, requests fall back to global coalesce path
Jamie: sounds like a soft-isolation layer. how do we avoid fragmentation of batch slots?
Alex: keep ephemeral windows as virtual lanes that don't reserve physical slots; they only mark requests with a tag and the batcher offers them into the next micro-window. fragmentation avoided because we don't carve GPU resources until the bundle is formed
Maria: what about observable signals? need clear metrics for eviction and fallback rates so product can tune tenant policies
Alex: agreed. propose: counters for ephemeral-created, ephemeral-evicted, fallback-rate, avg-latency-when-evicted. also histograms for window-fill times
Devon: runtime concern — KV cache pinning. if ephemeral requests trigger KV population then get evicted, we pay token cost twice
Priya: could attach a KV-pop hint: ephemeral requests use transient KV keys with TTL shorter than main path. TTL plus eviction reduces thrash
Jamie: edge-case: a tenant that always hovers near SLO but occasionally spikes. We can't keep flipping ephemeral on/off every spike
Alex: plan to use hysteresis: enable ephemeral for tenant after 3 spikes in a minute, disable after 5m of calm. config-driven
Maria: can we expose a per-tenant allowlist to always opt-in to ephemeral lanes? some partners may prefer degraded but predictable latency
Alex: yes. allowlist + priority score. default off for new tenants
Devon: small nit: need escape hatch for tail-latency debugging — capture a microtrace when fallback occurs more than X%
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: batcher/ephemeral-shim v0.1 -> staging at 2026-03-22T02:00Z :rocket:
Priya: one more — how about admission fairness? ephemeral should not let a low-paying tenant crowd out reserved capacity for paid customers
Alex: ephemeral is a low-tier admission cost: will not preempt reserved capacity; only borrows from best-effort pool. reserved pool check in admission path
Jamie: code sketch for admission gate:
```
if (tenant.isReserved()) -> route to reserved_queue
else if (tenant.onAllowlist) -> try_ephemeral_lane()
else -> best_effort_queue
```
Priya: ok, next steps: 1) formalize invariants in an RFC followup, 2) telemetry spec, 3) small staging rollout with canary tenants. i'll own telemetry doc
Alex: thanks — i'll put up an RFC draft and add the config proto example. cc @Maria for partner opt-in flow
Maria: noted. i'll sync with partner-eng on the allowlist UX
Devon: and i'll prototype the transient KV hint TTL change to measure thrash cost
Alex: sweet. TL;DR: ephemeral-window shim = low-risk isolation for bursty tenants, config + hysteresis + TTL hints + telemetry. trying to avoid core coalescer churn :thumbsup:
